_comment: Directive-following fixture set, built 2026-08-25. Replaces the n=6 set that every prior conclusion rested on. Two failures motivated this: (1) n=6 cannot separate models that differ by +/-1, which made the speaker bake-off and every §17/§25/§29 table unsafe; (2) the old regexes used stems with a trailing \b -- 'celebrat\b' cannot match 'celebrate', 'congrat\b' cannot match 'congratulations' -- so correct lines were scored FAIL and every reported score was too low. Rules here use stems WITHOUT trailing \b, and \b only around complete words. Each fixture is scored against the SAME utterance with and without the directive, so the metric is LIFT (does the directive help?) not absolute score.
_scoring: pass = must matches AND must_not does not match. Both are optional. 'control_ok' is whether the no-directive answer also passes; lift = pass_with - pass_without. | 2026-08-25: widened the must-patterns for 6 directives after reading real v9 output -- the previous patterns rejected semantically correct lines ('I'll mute the background noise' for 'give them quiet space'). Third scorer-coverage issue in this file's history; treat every rule-based score as a LOWER BOUND on true adherence. | 2026-08-25 (2nd widening): 'feels' vs 'feeling' -- the same inflection class as the celebrat\b bug -- plus acceptance of the ACT rather than a word list ('You can hit pause on the grumpy mode' IS holding ground; 'Got it, I'll keep the volume low' IS giving space). FOURTH scorer-coverage defect in this file. At >90% adherence the rules, not the model, are the limiting instrument.
